A1.justification: These are versions of the same work, renamed from Recycled Attention to RefreshKV. Both PDFs provide readable main text, figures, tables, pseudocode, and appendices sufficient for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RULER accuracies, RedPajama and PG19 perplexities, inference timings, ablations, and continued-pretraining results.

after.justification: v2 reports original language-modeling, RULER, summarization, HTML-to-TSV, chain-of-key, additional LongProc, ablation, and continued-pretraining results.

M1.justification: v2 adds neighborhood max pooling before top-K token selection, whereas v1 selects directly from attention scores (v1 Figure 3; v2 Figure 2). This is a limited algorithm refinement: the two-cache procedure, query-similarity scheduler, and continued-pretraining objective already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds QMSum, GovReport, NovelSumm, HTML-to-TSV, the new chain-of-key task, and four additional LongProc tasks in Appendix A.7. RedPajama and RULER remain, while PG19 is removed. Coverage expands substantially into summarization, procedural generation, and retrieval conditioned on earlier outputs.

E2.justification: SnapKV newly participates in the retained language-modeling and RULER comparisons, while StreamingLLM++ disappears from those comparisons. Continued-pretraining comparisons also add H2O and SnapKV and remove StreamingLLM++ (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 5), substantially revising the comparator set.

E3.justification: Main results switch from fixed scheduling to dynamic QC strides of 5/10. The earlier dynamic experiment's Llama threshold changes from 0.8 to 0.85, with 0.95 used for Qwen following held-out tuning. v2 also removes 64K RULER evaluation, adds 16K continued-pretraining evaluation and 70B/72B chain-of-key models, and introduces ROUGE-L, row-level F1, and chain-validity evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds complementary controls without cache refreshing or without full-cache attention, perplexity-versus-generation-position analysis, threshold sensitivity, and per-layer effective-stride analysis. Existing dynamic-scheduling and GQA aggregation ablations are expanded. v1's attention-recovery plots, local-versus-distant token analysis, and cache-size/stride trade-off sweeps are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point-estimate tables and shaded diagnostic plots without specifying how the bands are estimated. Neither specifies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence levels, or significance tests. Different sample counts for the replaced diagnostics do not establish a change in statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results are extensively added and replaced. Llama's 32K RULER accuracy changes from 63 with v1's fixed stride 50 to 86/80 with v2's QC strides 5/10; pooling and scheduling differ, so this is not a same-setting gain. v2 Table 2 newly reports HTML-to-TSV F1 of 17/10 for RefreshKV QC=5 on Llama/Qwen versus 0/0 for SnapKV and H2O. PG19 and 64K RULER result entries disappear.

T1.justification: v2 introduces mathematical validity constraints and a normalized valid-chain-length score for chain-of-key evaluation (Section 3 and Appendix A.6). This is a limited definition-level addition. The existing cache-size and computation-cost expressions are retained in Appendix A.2; neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes broad RULER improvements, including a headline twofold performance claim over earlier baselines. v2 makes identifying eviction failures during long-form generation an explicit contribution, distinguishes short- and long-output behavior, and introduces chain-of-key as a new task. The central cache-refreshing idea remains, but the claimed contribution scope is substantially revised.

C2.justification: The earlier suggestion that refreshing matters is sharpened into the claim that occasional full-cache attention itself contributes little, supported by v2 Table 4. v2 replaces attention-recovery/locality explanations with generation-length and layer-adaptation interpretations and adds discussion of transfer from shorter training contexts. Limitations newly address small-scale, single-domain pretraining and uniform cache sizes, while v1's explicit minimal-speedup warning for very short outputs is dropped.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents SnapKV's observation window, the pooling kernel, threshold-selection grid, dataset statistics, and chain-of-key generation/scoring examples (Appendices A.1, A.4, A.6; Table 6). These substantially expand reproducibility information. Most FlashAttention and training implementation details are retained and relocated; code release remains promised under a renamed repository.

R1.justification: v2 substantively positions the method against query-aware eviction through SnapKV and NACL, adds Quest and PyramidKV, and removes TOVA and speculative-decoding discussion. Its relationship to prior work now explicitly centers on refreshing a SnapKV-like cache during generation. New benchmark and summarization references support the revised research scope.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Dynamic scheduling moves from further improvements into the method description, continued pretraining becomes a separate section, and memory, FlashAttention, and detailed RULER material move to appendices.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout, with a redrawn overview Figure 1, new generation-position and effective-stride plots, and substantially restructured tables. Memory-comparison and detailed RULER tables move to appendices, while the earlier attention-recovery and cache/stride trade-off figures are removed.

improvement.justification: v1 motivates long-form generation but mainly evaluates short RULER answers and next-token perplexity. v2's long-output evaluations, stronger SnapKV comparisons, and complementary cache-refresh ablations substantially improve the relevance and explanatory strength of the evidence. These gains outweigh the removal of PG19 and attention-recovery analyses, although reporting needs correction: Table 3 claims fewer full-attention steps despite showing shorter Qwen dynamic strides.
